verses.text: "I tell you for certain, anyone who does not enter the sheep pen through the gate, but climbs in some other way, is a thief and a robber.
The one who comes in through the gate is the shepherd of the sheep.
The gatekeeper opens the gate for him, and the sheep listen to his voice. He calls his own sheep by name and leads them out.
When he has brought out all his own sheep, he walks ahead of them, and his sheep follow him because they know his voice.
They will never follow a stranger. In fact, they will run away from him, because they do not know a stranger's voice."
Jesus told them this picture story, but they did not understand what he was telling them.
So Jesus spoke again: "I tell you for certain, I am the gate for the sheep.
All who came before me were thieves and robbers, but the sheep did not listen to them.
I am the gate. Whoever comes in through me will be saved. They will come in and go out and find good pasture.
The thief comes only to steal, kill and destroy. I have come so that they may have life, and have it in all its fullness.
I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd gives up his life for the sheep.
A hired worker is not the shepherd, and the sheep do not belong to him. So when he sees a wolf coming, he leaves the sheep and runs away. Then the wolf attacks the flock and scatters it.
The man runs away because he is only working for money and does not really care about the sheep.
I am the good shepherd. I know my own sheep, and my own sheep know me,
just as the Father knows me and I know the Father. And I give up my life for the sheep.
I have other sheep too, which are not in this sheep pen. I must bring them also. They too will listen to my voice, and there will be one flock and one shepherd.
The Father loves me because I give up my life, so that I may take it back again.
No one takes it from me. I give it up of my own free will. I have the authority to give it up, and I have the authority to take it back again. This is what my Father has commanded me to do."
Once again the Jewish people were divided because of what Jesus said.
Many of them said, "He has a demon and is out of his mind. Why listen to him?"
But others said, "These are not the words of a man who has a demon. Can a demon open the eyes of the blind?"
Then came the Festival of Dedication in Jerusalem. It was winter,
and Jesus was walking in the temple courts, in the covered walkway called Solomon's Porch.
The Jewish leaders gathered round him and said, "How long will you keep us guessing? If you are the Christ, tell us plainly."
Jesus answered, "I did tell you, but you do not believe. The works I do in my Father's name speak for me.
But you do not believe, because you are not my sheep.
My sheep listen to my voice. I know them, and they follow me.
I give them eternal life, and they will never be lost. No one can snatch them out of my hand.
My Father, who has given them to me, is greater than all. No one can snatch them out of my Father's hand.
I and the Father are one."
Again the Jewish leaders picked up stones to stone him.
But Jesus said to them, "I have shown you many good works from the Father. For which of these are you going to stone me?"
They replied, "We are not stoning you for any good work, but for insulting God. You are only a man, but you are claiming to be God."
Jesus answered them, "Is it not written in your own law that God said, 'I have said that you are gods'?
God called them 'gods', those people to whom his message came, and the Scriptures cannot be set aside.
Then what about the one whom the Father set apart as his own and sent into the world? Why do you accuse me of insulting God because I said, 'I am the Son of God'?
Do not believe me unless I do the works of my Father.
But if I do them, even if you do not believe me, believe the works. Then you will know and understand that the Father is in me, and I am in the Father."
Again they tried to arrest him, but he escaped from their hands.
Then Jesus went back across the Jordan River to the place where John had first been baptising, and he stayed there.
Many people came to him. They said, "John never did a miraculous sign, but everything John said about this man was true."
And in that place many people believed in Jesus.
